description: Graduate treatment of digital transmission over noisy, dispersive and fading channels: optimal detection, modulation performance, equalisation, synchronisation, coding, OFDM and MIMO. In the lab students derive error rates, then build and validate a link-level simulation that reproduces theory and a published result.
modelledOn: Tse and Viswanath, Fundamentals of Wireless Communication
Moon, Error Correction Coding: Mathematical Methods and Algorithms
outcomes: Derive optimal receivers and error-probability bounds for signals in additive Gaussian noise using signal-space methods.
Compare modulation formats by bit error rate, spectral efficiency and robustness to fading.
Design and simulate equalisers and carrier and timing recovery loops for dispersive channels.
Evaluate channel codes against capacity limits, including convolutional, turbo, LDPC and polar codes.
Analyse and simulate OFDM and MIMO links, including diversity, multiplexing and precoding trade-offs.
Build a validated Monte Carlo link simulator and report results with confidence intervals against theory.

units.title: Signal space and detection theory
topics: Gram-Schmidt orthonormalisation and the vector representation of signals and constellations
The AWGN channel, sufficient statistics, correlator and matched-filter receivers
Hypothesis testing: MAP and ML detection, decision regions and Bayes risk
Union bound and nearest-neighbour approximation for error probability
Q-function, Eb/N0 versus Es/N0 and bit error rate definitions
Noncoherent detection with random phase; Rayleigh and Rician envelopes
Maximum-likelihood estimation and the Cramer-Rao bound for phase and timing

units.title: Modulation and demodulation performance
topics: PAM, PSK and QAM: exact and approximate error rates, Gray mapping
Orthogonal signalling, FSK, MSK and continuous-phase modulation: spectrum and efficiency
Differential and noncoherent schemes: DPSK and noncoherent FSK
Pulse shaping: the Nyquist criterion, raised-cosine and root-raised-cosine filters, eye diagrams
Performance in fading: Rayleigh and Rician average BER, outage and link budgets for mobile networks

units.title: Equalisation and synchronisation
topics: Intersymbol interference, the discrete-time equivalent channel and the whitened matched filter
Zero-forcing and MMSE linear equalisers and noise enhancement
Decision-feedback and maximum-likelihood sequence equalisation; adaptive LMS and RLS algorithms
Carrier phase recovery: phase-locked loops, the Costas loop and decision-directed methods
Symbol timing recovery: early-late gate and zero-crossing timing error detectors
Frame synchronisation, preambles and training sequences; frequency offset estimation

units.title: Channel coding and capacity limits
topics: Shannon capacity of the AWGN channel, the -1.59 dB limit and binary-input capacity
Linear block codes: generator and parity-check matrices, syndrome decoding, BCH and Reed-Solomon codes
Convolutional codes: trellis, hard and soft Viterbi decoding, free distance
Turbo codes and iterative MAP decoding
LDPC codes: Tanner graphs, belief propagation and density evolution
Polar codes: channel polarisation and successive-cancellation decoding
Coded modulation, coding gain and hybrid ARQ

units.title: OFDM and multicarrier systems
topics: Multicarrier principle, subcarrier orthogonality and FFT implementation
Cyclic prefix, guard interval and one-tap frequency-domain equalisation
Peak-to-average power ratio, clipping, selective mapping and amplifier nonlinearity
Preamble-based timing and frequency offset estimation; pilot-aided channel estimation
Bit loading, water-filling and adaptive modulation
OFDMA, SC-FDMA and the numerology of Wi-Fi, LTE and 5G NR

units.title: MIMO and diversity
topics: Time, frequency and space diversity; selection, equal-gain and maximal-ratio combining; diversity order
Two-antenna orthogonal space-time block codes and space-time trellis codes
The MIMO channel model, capacity, singular value decomposition and water-filling
Spatial multiplexing receivers: ZF, MMSE, successive interference cancellation and sphere decoding
The diversity-multiplexing trade-off
Beamforming, precoding and massive MIMO with channel hardening

units.title: Link-level simulation
topics: Monte Carlo BER estimation: sample size, confidence intervals and importance sampling
Building a simulation chain from source to BER counter in baseband-equivalent form
Channel models: AWGN, flat Rayleigh, tapped delay line and Doppler spectra
Validation against theory, seeds, vectorisation and reproducibility
Link adaptation, BLER-versus-SNR curves and throughput

units.title: Reproduction, design and research critique
topics: Reproducing a published BER result and quantifying the mismatch
Link design for rural broadband and TV white space in Africa
Capstone: designing and tuning a coded OFDM link to a throughput target
Open problems: short-packet communication, massive access and non-terrestrial links

schedule.title: Signal space, matched filters and MAP detection
schedule.exercise: Represent a four-signal set in signal space, derive the matched-filter output SNR, and bound the symbol error rate with the union bound.

tasks.title: Apply Gram-Schmidt to four given waveforms, find an orthonormal basis, and plot each signal as a point in signal space
Simulate BPSK over AWGN with a matched filter at Eb/N0 from 0 to 10 dB and plot measured BER against the Q-function theory
Implement the MAP decision rule for unequal priors with 8-ary signals, plot the decision regions, and show how they shift as the priors change

schedule.title: Error rates, noncoherent detection and estimation
schedule.exercise: Convert between Eb/N0, Es/N0 and SNR, derive the noncoherent FSK error probability, and compute a Cramer-Rao bound for phase estimation.

tasks.title: Convert between Eb/N0, Es/N0 and SNR for QPSK and 16-QAM at four bandwidth settings and tabulate the Eb/N0 needed for a BER of 1e-5
Simulate noncoherent binary FSK in noise and compare the measured BER with the exact expression 0.5 exp(-Eb/2N0)
Estimate a carrier phase offset by maximum likelihood from 200 noisy samples, compute the Cramer-Rao bound, and show the variance approaches it as SNR rises

schedule.title: Modulation formats, pulse shaping and fading
schedule.exercise: Compare PSK, QAM and FSK by SNR needed and bandwidth used, sketch an eye diagram, and estimate the average BER of QPSK in Rayleigh fading.

tasks.title: Plot the theoretical symbol error probability of 4, 16 and 64-QAM against Eb/N0 and read off the SNR penalty for each doubling of constellation size
Simulate DPSK and coherent BPSK over AWGN and measure the SNR penalty of differential detection at BER 1e-4, expecting about 1 dB
Generate a root-raised-cosine pulse train with roll-off 0.25 and 0.5, plot the eye diagram and power spectrum, and measure the occupied bandwidth
Simulate 16-QAM over Rayleigh flat fading, compute the average BER, compare it with the closed form, and estimate outage probability for a 10 dB threshold

schedule.title: Linear equalisation and the ISI channel
schedule.exercise: Compute the output SNR of zero-forcing and MMSE equalisers for a two-path channel, and explain when maximum-likelihood sequence detection is worth its cost.

tasks.title: Convolve a symbol sequence with a three-tap ISI channel, plot the received samples, and show how ISI closes the eye opening for BPSK
Design zero-forcing and MMSE linear equalisers with 11 taps for a given channel, and compare output SNR and noise enhancement at 5 and 15 dB
Implement a trellis-search sequence detector for a 3-tap channel, compare its BER with a decision-feedback equaliser at 8 dB, and explain the gap

schedule.title: Carrier, timing and frame synchronisation
schedule.exercise: Choose the loop bandwidth of a carrier-tracking loop trading noise against tracking speed, and design a preamble for reliable frame detection.

tasks.title: Correlate a received signal with a known preamble to locate the frame start, and measure detection probability at 0, -3 and -6 dB SNR
Build a second-order phase-locked loop for QPSK carrier recovery, choose its bandwidth, and plot phase error as it locks onto a 1 kHz offset
Implement early-late gate timing recovery for oversampled root-raised-cosine BPSK with a 100 ppm clock offset, and plot timing error and BER

schedule.title: Capacity and block, convolutional codes
schedule.exercise: Compute the minimum Eb/N0 for a given spectral efficiency, decode a Hamming word by syndrome, and trace Viterbi decoding on a short trellis.

tasks.title: Plot AWGN channel capacity and binary-input AWGN capacity against SNR, and mark the Eb/N0 limit of -1.59 dB at zero spectral efficiency
Build Hamming(7,4) and (15,11) encoders with syndrome decoders and compare coded and uncoded BER over a binary symmetric channel at crossover 0.001 to 0.1
Implement soft-decision Viterbi decoding for a rate-1/2, constraint length 3 convolutional code and measure the coding gain over hard decisions at BER 1e-4

schedule.title: Modern codes: turbo, LDPC, polar and HARQ
schedule.exercise: Run bit-flipping decoding on a Tanner graph, choose frozen bits for an (8,4) polar code, and compare codes by the Eb/N0 each needs at BER 1e-5.

tasks.title: Draw the Tanner graph of a small parity-check matrix, run bit-flipping decoding on a word with two errors, and record which checks fail at each round
Construct an (8,4) polar code by ranking synthetic channels for frozen bits, and decode it with successive cancellation over AWGN
Implement a two-branch turbo decoder with log-MAP component decoders and plot BER over 1 to 8 iterations at 1 dB
Compare the Eb/N0 needed at BER 1e-5 for uncoded, Hamming, convolutional and LDPC codes from supplied curves, and rank them by coding gain and rate loss

schedule.title: OFDM fundamentals and the cyclic prefix
schedule.exercise: Show why a cyclic prefix turns a multipath channel into parallel flat subchannels, and size the prefix for a given delay spread.

tasks.title: Build an OFDM symbol with 64 subcarriers using an inverse FFT, plot the waveform and spectrum, and confirm orthogonality by recovering each subcarrier
Add a cyclic prefix, pass the symbol through a 4-tap multipath channel, equalise with one tap per subcarrier, and plot BER with and without the prefix
Measure the PAPR distribution for 64 and 256 subcarriers, reduce it with clipping and filtering, and report the BER penalty

schedule.title: OFDM estimation, loading and standards
schedule.exercise: Estimate a channel from pilots, allocate power across subcarriers by water-filling, and compare the numerology of Wi-Fi, LTE and 5G NR.

tasks.title: Apply water-filling to eight subcarriers of known gains and a power budget, and compute the capacity gain over equal power
Estimate the channel from pilot subcarriers by least squares with linear interpolation, and plot MSE against pilot spacing at 15 dB
Compare the subcarrier spacing, symbol duration and cyclic prefix of Wi-Fi, LTE and 5G NR from supplied parameters, and compute each one's tolerable delay spread
Estimate and correct carrier frequency offset in OFDM using a repeated training symbol, showing BER with offsets of 0.1, 0.3 and 0.5 subcarrier spacings

schedule.title: Diversity combining and space-time codes
schedule.exercise: Derive the diversity order of maximal-ratio combining, show that a two-antenna space-time code achieves second-order diversity, and compute MIMO capacity.

tasks.title: Simulate selection, equal-gain and maximal-ratio combining with 1, 2 and 4 branches in Rayleigh fading, and read the diversity order from the BER slopes
Implement the two-antenna orthogonal space-time block code encoder and combiner, and measure its 3 dB loss against 1x2 combining at equal total transmit power
Compute ergodic capacity of 2x2, 4x4 and 8x8 Rayleigh MIMO channels by Monte Carlo and compare with the singular value and water-filling prediction at 10 dB

schedule.title: Spatial multiplexing and massive MIMO
schedule.exercise: Compare ZF, MMSE and successive-cancellation receivers for a 2x2 link, and explain how massive MIMO makes the channel nearly deterministic.

tasks.title: Compare zero-forcing and MMSE detection for a 2x2 spatial multiplexing link with 4-QAM and plot BER from 0 to 20 dB
Estimate the diversity-multiplexing trade-off for a 2x2 system from simulated outage probability at several rates, and compare it with the ideal curve
Simulate a base station with 64 antennas serving four users by zero-forcing precoding, and show channel hardening and sum-rate growth as antennas increase

schedule.title: Building a link-level simulator
schedule.exercise: Plan a simulation chain, decide how many bits are needed for a BER of 1e-6, and validate your simulator against two closed-form results.

tasks.title: Run a BPSK Monte Carlo simulation with 1e3, 1e5 and 1e6 bits at 8 dB and compute a 95 percent confidence interval for each BER estimate
Implement a tapped-delay-line channel from a given power-delay profile with Jakes Doppler, and verify the simulated Doppler spectrum and delay spread against targets
Plot BLER and throughput against SNR for six modulation-and-coding settings, and pick the best setting per SNR as a link-adaptation table
Build a modular link chain with source, coder, modulator, channel, receiver and BER counter, with configuration and unit tests, and reproduce a published BER curve within 0.2 dB

schedule.title: Reproduction, rural link design and open problems
schedule.exercise: Reproduce a published BER curve, design a rural fixed link with a link budget, and write a one-page critique naming one open problem.

tasks.title: Compute the link budget for a 20 km rural fixed link with margin for rain and fading, and find the highest modulation order meeting BER 1e-6
Reproduce a BER curve from a described paper using its parameters, list each assumption you had to guess, and quantify the mismatch
Design, simulate and tune a coded OFDM link to meet 5 Mbit/s at BER 1e-5 in a 5 MHz channel over a fading profile, and report the trade-offs
